Issues.Title: ItemsControl with VirtualizingStackPanel scrolls when clicking the last visible CheckBox item
Issues.Body:
### Description

Clicking the CheckBox of the last visible item in an ItemsControl does not immediately toggle its checked state. Instead, the content scrolls and brings additional items into view. 
This behavior occurs when the ItemsControl is hosted within a ScrollViewer and uses a VirtualizingStackPanel, making interaction with the bottom-most visible item inconsistent compared to other visible items.


### Reproduction Steps

## Please find the sample to replicate the issue: ##

[ItemsControlSample.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32797516/ItemsControlSample.zip)

## Replication Procedure:
1. Run the sample.
2. Click the checkbox of the last row in the view port.

## Video Reference
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c23c2258-5193-4238-9474-f693bfa64688

### Expected behavior

A single click on last value in the viewport should directly toggle the checkbox state without causing any scrolling.

### Actual behavior

Clicking the CheckBox of the last visible item in the viewport does not toggle the CheckBox state. Instead, the ScrollViewer automatically scrolls and brings additional items into view.

### Regression?

### Configuration

.NET version -> .NET framework 4.8.1
OS version -> Windows 11 Enterprise & Version - 24H2

Issues.Title: Add WindowChrome DWM caption/backdrop support
Issues.Body:
Introduce modern DWM-driven window chrome: add CaptionTextColorHelper and WindowCaptionAdorner; extend WindowChrome with new enums/properties (FrameMode, CaptionTheme, BackdropType, CornerPreference, caption/border/text colors) and read-only attached properties for per-window state. Rewrite WindowChromeWorker to manage extended-client-area, DWM attributes, backdrop, DPI-aware frame insets, caption buttons and adorner. Expand NativeMethods and Utilities for new DWM/monitor/AppBar APIs. Remove legacy WindowBackdropManager and WindowBackdropType. Integrate with ThemeManager and update Ribbon templates to use WindowChrome extended mode. Add comprehensive unit tests for caption color, frame insets and WindowChrome behavior. Update project includes and internals visibility for tests.

Fixes #11973 11973

## Description

Introduces modern DWM-driven window chrome integration for WindowChrome:
- New CaptionTextColorHelper and WindowCaptionAdorner
- New WindowChrome properties/enums: FrameMode, CaptionTheme, BackdropType, CornerPreference, caption/border/text colors, plus read-only attached properties for per-window state
- WindowChromeWorker rewritten to manage extended client area, DWM attributes, backdrop, DPI-aware frame insets, caption buttons and the adorner
- Expanded NativeMethods/Utilities for the new DWM/monitor/AppBar APIs
- Removed legacy WindowBackdropManager/WindowBackdropType
- Ribbon templates and ThemeManager updated to use the new extended chrome mode
- Added unit tests for caption color, frame insets and WindowChrome behavior

## Customer Impact

Enables apps to opt into native Mica/Acrylic backdrops, rounded corner preference, and DWM-driven caption/border theming without custom chrome hacks.

## Regression

No known regressions have been observed when the new opt-in properties are not used. Because this change substantially updates `WindowChromeWorker`, additional review and testing are still needed for existing custom-chrome scenarios.

## Testing

Added unit tests for the managed property and frame-inset behavior. Native DWM behavior, rendering, DPI transitions, and caption-button interaction were manually verified on Windows 11 (including dpi and high contrast theme).

## Risk

Touches `WindowChromeWorker` internals broadly. The changes are covered by unit tests where practical and are gated behind new opt-in properties. Some behavior, including native DWM integration, rendering, DPI transitions, and caption-button interaction, requires manual validation on supported Windows configurations.

Issues.Title: [API Proposal]: WindowChrome extensions for system frame integration, DWM caption/border colors, corner preference, backdrop and extended client area
Issues.Body:
### Background and motivation `System.Windows.Shell.WindowChrome` currently only supports **fully custom chrome**: WPF paints the whole non-client area itself and the system frame is not involved beyond hit-testing/resizing. This proposal extends `WindowChrome` with two more first-class modes — keeping the **system frame** while only customizing its DWM appearance (colors, corners, theme, backdrop), and an **extended client area** mode where the system caption buttons stay live while WPF content flows under/around them (similar to WinUI 3's `ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar`). It also exposes the modern DWM window attributes (caption/text/border color, corner preference, dark caption, Mica/Acrylic/Tabbed backdrop) as bindable properties, and adds read-only attached properties that let arbitrary content correctly avoid or align with the system-drawn caption buttons. This closes long-standing gaps where custom-titlebar WPF apps had to either fully reimplement the caption buttons (losing snap-layout flyouts, accessibility, and touch/keyboard behavior) or fall back to raw P/Invoke to get Windows 11 Mica/Acrylic, dark titlebars, or rounded corners. It also formalizes (as public, documented API) backdrop/immersive-dark-mode behavior that today exists only as private support for the Fluent theme (`WindowBackdropManager`, `Window.SetImmersiveDarkMode`, both internal). Property reference Property | Type | Values / meaning | Default -- | -- | -- | -- `FrameMode` | `WindowChromeFrameMode` | `Custom` — WPF fully owns the non-client area; `ExtendedClientArea` — system frame/buttons stay active, client area extends under the caption; `SystemFrame` — system frame untouched, only caption appearance/backdrop are managed. | `Custom` `ShowSystemIcon` | `bool?` | `true` shows the system icon; `false` hides it; `null` defers to `FrameMode`: shown in `Custom`/`SystemFrame`, hidden in `ExtendedClientArea`. | `null` `ShowTitle` | `bool?` | `true` shows the title; `false` hides it; `null` defers to `FrameMode`: shown in `Custom`/`SystemFrame`, hidden in `ExtendedClientArea`. | `null` `CaptionColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; alpha ignored **unless** a backdrop is active, in which case a fully transparent color asks DWM not to paint the caption at all so the backdrop shows through even when the system is set to color titlebars (`DWMWA_COLOR_NONE`). `null` restores the system-chosen caption color. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `CaptionTextColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; alpha channel ignored. `null` restores the system-chosen text color. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `BorderColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; `null` restores the default border; a color with alpha `0` removes the border. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `CornerPreference` | `WindowCornerPreference` | `Default` — system choice; `DoNotRound`; `Round`; `RoundSmall` — smaller radius. Requires Windows 11. | `Default` `CaptionTheme` | `WindowCaptionTheme` | `Auto` — follows Fluent/framework theme, otherwise system; `Light`; `Dark`. Requires Windows 10 1809+. | `Auto` `BackdropType` | `WindowBackdropKind` | `Auto` — Mica for Fluent windows, none otherwise; `None`; `Mica`; `Acrylic`; `Tabbed` — Mica Alt. Requires Windows 11 22H2+. | `Auto` `CaptionButtonsBounds` | `Rect`, read-only attached | Rect in DIPs, relative to client origin, occupied by the system caption buttons; `default(Rect)` if the system isn't drawing them over the client area. | `default(Rect)` `CaptionButtonsClip` | `Geometry`, read-only attached | Frozen geometry covering the whole client area except `CaptionButtonsBounds`, meant to be bound to an element's `Clip` so it never paints over the caption buttons; expressed in client-origin coordinates (not suitable for nested/offset elements). `null` when the system isn't drawing the buttons over the client area. | `null` `TitleBarBounds` | `Rect`, read-only attached | Rect in DIPs for app content within the caption band, excluding `CaptionButtonsBounds`; `default(Rect)` when not applicable. | `default(Rect)` `CaptionForeground` | `Brush`, read-only attached | Brush computed by system/framework for caption text, accounting for active state, accent color, theme, and `CaptionColor`/`CaptionTextColor`. | `SystemColors.ActiveCaptionTextBrush` `IsCaptionCustomizationSupported` | `bool`, static read-only | `true` on Windows 11+; otherwise `false`. | OS-dependent `IsBackdropSupported` | `bool`, static read-only | `true` on Windows 11 22H2+; otherwise `false`. | OS-dependent

 

(written with help of AI — in case the suspiciously tidy formatting 🤖) ### API Proposal ```csharp namespace System.Windows.Shell; public enum WindowChromeFrameMode { Custom = 0, // WPF fully owns the non-client area (existing/default behavior) ExtendedClientArea = 1, // system frame + buttons stay active; client area extends under the caption SystemFrame = 2, // system frame untouched; only caption appearance/backdrop are managed } public enum WindowCornerPreference { Default = 0, DoNotRound = 1, Round = 2, RoundSmall = 3, } public enum WindowCaptionTheme { Auto = 0, Light = 1, Dark = 2, } public enum WindowBackdropKind { Auto = 0, None = 1, Mica = 2, Acrylic = 3, Tabbed = 4, } public class WindowChrome : Freezable { // New instance properties public WindowChromeFrameMode FrameMode { get; set; } // default: Custom public bool? ShowSystemIcon { get; set; } // default: null public bool? ShowTitle { get; set; } // default: null public Color? CaptionColor { get; set; } // default: null public Color? CaptionTextColor { get; set; } // default: null public Color? BorderColor { get; set; } // default: null public WindowCornerPreference CornerPreference { get; set; } // default: Default public WindowCaptionTheme CaptionTheme { get; set; } // default: Auto public WindowBackdropKind BackdropType { get; set; } // default: Auto // New static/read-only helpers public static bool IsCaptionCustomizationSupported { get; } // Windows 11+ public static bool IsBackdropSupported { get; } // Windows 11 22H2+ // New read-only attached properties (set by the framework on the Window) public static Rect GetCaptionButtonsBounds(DependencyObject element); public static Geometry GetCaptionButtonsClip(DependencyObject element); public static Rect GetTitleBarBounds(DependencyObject element); public static Brush GetCaptionForeground(DependencyObject element); // Corresponding DependencyProperty fields for all of the above } ``` ### API Usage ```xaml ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_

Issues.Title: Regression in Clipboard/DataObject text conversion
Issues.Body:
### Description

The text in clipboard/data object seems to be no longer auto-converted between Text and UnicodeText format.

### Reproduction Steps

```C#
DataObject d = new DataObject();
d.SetText("ahoj", TextDataFormat.Text);

Clipboard.SetDataObject(d);

var present = Clipboard.GetDataObject().GetDataPresent("UnicodeText");
var hasText = Clipboard.ContainsText();
var hasUnicode = Clipboard.ContainsText(TextDataFormat.UnicodeText);
```

### Expected behavior

returns true for all calls, which is the case in .NET up to 9.0

### Actual behavior

returns false for all calls

### Regression?

yes, works in .NET 9 and before 

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Impact

Applications cannot access text in clipboard/drag data.

### Configuration

.NET 10.0.11
Windows 11 (x64 29667)

### Other information

@JeremyKuhne @merriemcgaw

Issues.Title: Fix: TabPanel row count during arrange
Issues.Body:
Recompute the horizontal row count from the current arrange inputs so header distribution arrays match the actual flow. Add regression coverage for a stale measure-time row count.

Fixes #11942

## Description
`TabPanel` could throw an `IndexOutOfRangeException` during horizontal arrangement when its cached measure-time row count no longer matched the rows required by the current arrange width and header sizes.
This change recalculates the row count at the beginning of `ArrangeHorizontal` using the same wrapping rules as `CalculateHeaderDistribution`. This ensures the distribution arrays are sized for the rows that arrangement will actually produce.

## Customer Impact
The exception is unhandled during WPF layout and can terminate the application, potentially causing customer data loss. The issue has been observed during tab-close transitions on both .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET 10.

## Regression

No.

## Testing

Added a deterministic unit test that:
• Measures headers with widths  [65, 35, 60]  at width  113 , producing two cached rows.
• Arranges them at width  76 , requiring three rows.
• Verifies arrangement completes and places the headers on three rows.

## Risk
Low.
The change is private and localized to horizontal `TabPanel` layout. When measure and arrange inputs agree, the recomputed row count is unchanged and existing behavior is preserved. Behavior changes only when the cached row count is inconsistent with the current arrange inputs.
The additional work is a single linear pass over the header widths during arrangement. No public API or vertical tab layout behavior is changed.

Issues.Title: Add MouseHorizontalWheel and PreviewMouseHorizontalWheel routed events
Issues.Body:
Fixes #3201

Main PR N/A

## Description

WPF exposes `PreviewMouseWheel` and `MouseWheel` for vertical wheel
 rotation, but has no equivalent routed events for horizontal wheel
 rotation.

Windows sends `WM_MOUSEHWHEEL` to the active window when the horizontal
 scroll wheel is tilted or rotated. `HwndMouseInputProvider` does not
 handle this message, so horizontal scroll input never reaches the UI
 through WPF's routed event system.

This change adds the missing routed events and wires them through the
 input pipeline and the scrollable controls.

The new events follow the same pattern as the existing vertical wheel
events:

- `HwndMouseInputProvider` handles `WM_MOUSEHWHEEL` alongside
  `WM_MOUSEWHEEL`, ~negates the wheel delta to match the direction
  convention, and~ reports it as
  `RawMouseActions.HorizontalWheelRotate`
- `MouseDevice` processes `RawMouseActions.HorizontalWheelRotate` and
  raises `PreviewMouseHorizontalWheel` / `MouseHorizontalWheel`
- `Mouse` registers `PreviewMouseHorizontalWheelEvent` /
  `MouseHorizontalWheelEvent` and exposes the `Add` / `Remove` handler
  methods
- `UIElement`, `UIElement3D`, and `ContentElement` expose the events
  and `OnMouseHorizontalWheel` / `OnPreviewMouseHorizontalWheel`
  virtual methods
- `ScrollViewer`, `TextBoxBase`, and `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` scroll
  horizontally in response

See: Win32 `WM_MOUSEHWHEEL`

## Customer Impact

Applications that want to support horizontal scrolling from a touchpad
or a tilt mouse wheel currently cannot receive the input through WPF.
With this change, horizontal wheel input flows through the standard
routed event system, so existing `ScrollViewer`-based controls scroll
horizontally out of the box.

## Regression

No. This is a new feature. The existing vertical wheel events and all
other input paths are unchanged.

## Testing

Built the WPF runtime packages with `build.cmd` in the Debug
configuration and referenced them from a separate application (WPF
Gallery) to validate the feature against a real WPF app.

Verified that:

- `WM_MOUSEHWHEEL` maps to `RawMouseActions.HorizontalWheelRotate`
- `PreviewMouseHorizontalWheel` and `MouseHorizontalWheel` fire in
  tunnel / bubble order
- `ScrollViewer`, `TextBoxBase`, and `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` scroll
  horizontally on the new event
- The API contract in `ref/PresentationCore.cs` matches the runtime
  implementation

## Risk

Low.

The change adds new events and a new message handler. Existing event
routing, vertical wheel handling, and the `RawMouseActions` enumeration
semantics are not modified.
